question: Does early initiation of statin therapy reduce 30-day mortality in patients presenting with acute coronary syndrome?
context: A retrospective cohort study of 8,432 patients admitted with ACS at three tertiary centres compared 30-day all-cause mortality between those started on high-intensity statin within 24 hours of admission and those started after 72 hours. Adjusted odds ratio for 30-day mortality was 0.63 (95% CI 0.51-0.78, p<0.001) favouring early initiation.
long_answer: Early high-intensity statin therapy was associated with a 37% relative reduction in 30-day mortality compared with delayed initiation. Effect was preserved across STEMI and NSTEMI subgroups.

question: Is metformin contraindicated in patients with eGFR 30-45 mL/min/1.73m2?
context: FDA label revision in 2016 raised the eGFR threshold from 60 to 30 mL/min/1.73m2. A meta-analysis of 12 trials (n=11,247) including patients with eGFR 30-60 found no statistically significant increase in lactic acidosis at the lower threshold (0.03 vs 0.04 events per 100 patient-years).
long_answer: Metformin is no longer contraindicated at eGFR 30-45 but dose should be reduced to maximum 1000mg/day and renal function monitored every 3-6 months. Below eGFR 30, metformin remains contraindicated.

question: Does the addition of dexamethasone to standard therapy reduce mortality in hospitalised COVID-19 patients requiring oxygen?
context: The RECOVERY trial (n=6,425) randomised hospitalised COVID-19 patients to dexamethasone 6mg daily for up to 10 days vs usual care. Among patients receiving oxygen, 28-day mortality was 23.3% vs 26.2% (RR 0.83, 95% CI 0.75-0.93, p<0.001).
long_answer: Dexamethasone significantly reduced 28-day mortality in patients requiring oxygen support (RR 0.83) and invasive mechanical ventilation (RR 0.64). No benefit was observed in patients not requiring oxygen.
